description: R08 Functional Closeout checkpoint: retire the complete TerminalApi family, the first two TerminalBuffer aggregate contracts, and the complete residual Selection family after Microsoft-derived product/witness validation.

entries.notes: Rust accepts Microsoft-valid color table indices 0, 128, and 255 and rejects 512 through the portable color-table owner.
Rust reproduces Microsoft's cursor blink/visibility state transitions, including simultaneous non-blinking hidden state.
Rust decodes and writes Microsoft's repeated surrogate-pair string while making deterministic forward progress beyond buffer width.
Rust opens, retains through text output, resolves, and closes the hyperlink identity used by Microsoft.
Rust reuses a hyperlink identity for the same custom id and URI exactly as Microsoft's contract requires.
Rust assigns distinct hyperlink identities when a custom id is reused with a different URI while preserving both mappings.
Rust mirrors Microsoft's reset, invalid-state rejection, clamp-to-100, indeterminate preservation, and minimum-progress behavior.
Rust accepts Microsoft-valid quoted/unquoted paths including Unicode and rejects empty or malformed quote payloads without mutating state.
Rust writes Microsoft's Hello World vector into the aggregate TextBuffer without moving the viewport.
Rust preserves a scrolled-back viewport while output advances and only converges toward the mutable viewport as history saturates.
Rust clamps extreme selection coordinates for unit, word, and line expansion across normal and maximum scrollback heights.
Rust converts viewport input to stable buffer coordinates before constructing the selection, reproducing Microsoft's scrolled selection geometry.
Rust clamps anchors entering from each out-of-bounds direction to the Microsoft terminal boundary.
Rust clamps moving selection endpoints on all four out-of-bounds directions while retaining pivot ordering.
Rust repairs an anchor placed on the trailing half of Microsoft's wide glyph to cover the complete glyph.
Rust expands block-selection boundaries independently per row when either boundary intersects a trailing wide-glyph cell.
